title: Comparing change goals and feasibility beliefs about changing social, emotional, and behavioral skills vs. personality traits among adolescents, parents, and teachers
issue_summary: Do BESSI-derived items repurposed to assess change goals/feasibility beliefs count as eligible SEB quantitative measurement?
ai_recommendation: Ineligible for meta-analysis because the measured construct is beliefs/goals about SEB skills rather than SEB skill level/capacity.
decision_options: eligible as modified BESSI;ineligible because target construct is not SEB skill level/capacity
review_evidence: [pp. 2-3] SEB vs trait change goals/feasibility are central.
meta_evidence: [p. 5] BESSI-45 items are systematically modified for change goals/feasibility beliefs.
adjudication_note: BESSI-derived content measures beliefs/change goals, not levels of SEB skills; therefore it is quantitatively ineligible.

title: Cognitive Abilities, Personality, and Sustainable Attitudes and Behavior
issue_summary: Which internal study components should proceed to quantitative coding?
ai_recommendation: Only Study 2 should proceed because it administers the BESSI-96; do not create a placeholder sample for Study 1.
decision_options: code Study 2 only;create placeholder for Study 1 and code Study 2
adjudication_note: Only Study 2 enters quantitative coding. Study 1 receives no sample_id or matrix_id.

title: From fragmentation to framework: defining core human competencies for higher education and the workplace
issue_summary: How should the paper's relationship to SEB/BESSI be preserved for later review topic coding?
ai_recommendation: Retain for review and explicitly tag as extending/modifying and comparing SEB/BESSI with other frameworks.
decision_options: generic review inclusion only;preserve framework extension/modification relation
review_evidence: [p. 1, p. 4] BESSI is synthesized and mapped into the proposed 4S framework.
meta_evidence: [p. 1] Conceptual/bibliometric paper without original BESSI participant data.
adjudication_note: Preserve explicitly that the paper extends/modifies and compares the SEB/BESSI framework when review topics are coded.
